verification_report.summary:
The corrected complete chapter is correct under the explicitly accepted local inputs. All 16 sequential statement checks and 5 reference checks passed with no critical errors or gaps. Connectedness is stated both in the chapter and in the book conventions, resolving the sole objection in envelope_testcurves_01. That historical report was preserved.

Both decreasing-limit arguments are valid: supremum-zero normalization on connected compact X gives a uniform L1 bound, and monotone convergence excludes collapse of Gamma_tau at the cutoff and of u_t-ct at infinity. The resulting raw limits are genuine canonical potentials. No general envelope idempotence, closure of model nets, or fixedness of Gamma_c is assumed.

Closed concave fibers and the restrictions t>0 and tau<c are justified, including boundary supporting slopes and identically minus-infinity fibers. Fubini, vertical convexity, canonical Kiselman inverse potentials, and pointwise reconstruction prove equality of the raw forward supremum with its product regularization at every point, including poles. The forward envelope identity uses order in both directions, and the L1 initial limit is established. Perron replacement is valid at all seams, including intervals starting at zero; its dual error is exactly bounded by (b-a)(c-tau). The reverse rooftop affine competitor proves P_theta[g]=g by first infimizing in M and then letting s decrease to zero. The initial-potential and cutoff arguments complete the bijection.

The completed hermitian_perron_rays_01 report is correct and supplies precisely the required nonclosed-background minimum principle, endpoint control and Perron constructions. Source comparisons confirm the local minimum principle in [SGPT, Proposition 1.2.8](https://mingchenxia.github.io/Lectures/SGPT.pdf) and elementary biconjugation in [Proposition 3.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1606.05235). No global mass-dependent geometry, E_env identification, automatic affine supremum for arbitrary rays, Darvas metric, or weak HCMA claim is imported.

The P1 example is correct with dd^c=i/(2pi) partial barpartial and FS integral one. Its model current is lambda*delta_0 plus FS on |z|^2>lambda/(1-lambda), with no joining-circle atom. The rotational envelope, secant-slope bound, tangent barrier and ordinary-type argument are valid. The maximizing parameter is e^t|z|^2/(1+e^t|z|^2), giving the stated smooth ray and values zero at zero and t at infinity. The figure only illustrates these formulas. The book was left unchanged.
